notes: ACCESS: tier (a) direct HTTP fetch (requests + Chrome UA) worked cleanly for robots.txt, homepage and all category pages; no block encountered, no need to escalate to Playwright or Claude-in-Chrome. robots.txt checked first: general Disallow list excludes /search/, /item/, pagination (?page=), etc. but allows /furniture/... category browse paths; ClaudeBot is listed with only Crawl-delay:1 (no Disallow), so tier (c) would also be permitted if needed, but was not required. TREE: built from homepage mega-menu hrefs (union with each category page's own sub-nav facet, since sitemap.xml returned 404). Site is a curated antiques/vintage/design marketplace organized entirely under /furniture/ as the single home-goods department, with top-level nodes Seating, Tables, Storage & Case Pieces, Lighting, Rugs and Carpets, Mirrors, Wall Decorations, Decorative Objects, and More Furniture & Collectibles (which contains Bedroom Furniture, Home Accents, and Textiles). QTY: every qty is the site's own rendered total, cross-verified two ways per page - the embedded GraphQL Apollo-state 'totalResults' field AND the human-visible page <title>/'X For Sale at 1stDibs' text plus the 'Search within X results' placeholder and facet-count badge - all three matched exactly on every recorded row. TEXTILE: 'Textiles' (More Furniture & Collectibles > Textiles) has exactly 3 sub-nav children with no further split - Pillows and Throws (9,649), Quilts and Blankets (933), Curtains and Valances (456) - all textile per rules (cushions/throws, quilts/blankets, curtains). 'Rugs and Carpets' is a separate top-level site category (rugs are Textile per textile.md SS6); it has ~30 regional/style sub-nav children (Turkish Rugs, Indian Rugs, Persian Rugs, etc.) that are all still just 'Rugs' by product type, so per the worker brief's efficiency guidance for this deep-tree marketplace I recorded the parent's own reliable rendered total (113,076) as a single row instead of enumerating every regional leaf, rather than expanding into ~30 near-identical rug-type rows. EXCLUDED: 'Storage & Case Pieces' (bookcases, cabinets, credenzas, dressers, wardrobes-armoires) is explicitly a Furniture-department category on the site (storage-furniture boundary, storage.md SS21/SS27) - out of scope for Storage.xlsx, already Furniture's domain. 'Decorative Objects > Bowls and Baskets' (and its own children Vases and Vessels, Sculptures, Desk Accessories, Boxes, Candle Holders) are antique/collectible decorative pieces, not functional storage products (storage.md SS5/SS23/SS24) - excluded. 'Wall Decorations' (Prints, Paintings, Decorative Art) has no tapestry/fabric-wall-hanging sub-node - excluded entirely, no textile match. No dedicated Storage/Organization department, no laundry/closet/office/kitchen storage nodes, no organizers exist anywhere in the site's nav - this is a high-end antiques marketplace, not a home-organization retailer, so storage_rows is empty (a valid, correct result, not a miss). No View-All/Collection/search-result/product-detail URLs used; no duplicates (each row backed by one canonical category URL only).
